audio_prompt: Which revision best removes an exclusionary appeal from “True fans stay until the final siren”?

answers.text: “Staying until the final siren can be one way fans show support.”
“Obviously true fans never leave early.”
“Only loyal people stay to the end.”
“We all know leaving early is betrayal.”

explanation.summary: The revision keeps the connection between staying and support but no longer makes one behaviour the test of authentic fandom.
explanation.hint: Keep the idea without policing membership.

subject: english
question: A speech says, “You and I may disagree on the route, but we both want safer streets.” What does the pronoun pattern accomplish?
audio_prompt: A speech says, “You and I may disagree on the route, but we both want safer streets.” What does the pronoun pattern accomplish?

answers.text: It acknowledges difference before constructing a narrower area of shared purpose
It pretends no disagreement exists
It excludes the speaker from the issue
It makes the claim impersonal

explanation.summary: “You and I” recognises separate positions, while “we both” creates alignment around a specific common goal.
explanation.hint: Notice the movement from difference to common ground.

subject: english
question: A campaign slogan reads, “This is our river. Its future is our choice.” Which feature carries most of the alignment work?
audio_prompt: A campaign slogan reads, “This is our river. Its future is our choice.” Which feature carries most of the alignment work?

answers.text: Repeated inclusive possessive “our”
The full stop
The word “future” alone
The absence of statistics

explanation.summary: Repeated “our” constructs shared ownership and responsibility, positioning the audience as part of the decision-making community.
explanation.hint: Track who is made to own both the place and the decision.

subject: english
question: A student article says, “Clearly, no one wants assessment to be unfair.” What is the best next analytical step?
audio_prompt: A student article says, “Clearly, no one wants assessment to be unfair.” What is the best next analytical step?

answers.text: Separate the broadly agreeable value of fairness from whatever policy claim the writer attaches to it next
Accept every later claim because fairness is good
Ignore “clearly” because it is only an adverb
Assume all readers define fairness identically

explanation.summary: Writers can establish easy shared ground and then use it to support a more contestable proposal; readers should test that connection.
explanation.hint: Agreement with a value does not automatically prove the next claim.
